title.en: Composite reinforcement direction and laminate edge

summary: Keep a composite surface pattern consistent with its declared reinforcement and show a separate authored laminate edge where layers are exposed.
objective: Keep a composite surface pattern consistent with its declared reinforcement and show a separate authored laminate edge where layers are exposed.
intent_signals: Keep a composite surface pattern consistent with its declared reinforcement and show a separate authored laminate edge where layers are exposed.
example_prompts: Build an explorable composite reinforcement direction and laminate edge and expose its construction at close range.

principles: A checkerboard weave is not a universal carbon-fiber appearance. The cited manufacturer supplies both woven and unidirectional reinforcement forms.
Choose a display specimen with a declared reinforcement type and an authored resin-rich outer finish. Surface appearance does not reveal the entire internal layup or establish mechanical strength.
implementation: Create a thin panel or curved shell with finite thickness, a trim edge and any actual mounting holes. For an explanatory edge inset store a list of plies with orientation and thickness; derive the stack height from their sum. This list is an authored teaching layup, not a certified design.

For a woven outer ply give the two interlaced bundle directions a coherent local pattern; for a unidirectional outer ply emphasize one direction rather than reusing a checker texture. Keep texture coordinates attached to each panel and disclose deliberate cosmetic discontinuities at joins.

Separate outer resin/clear-finish response from reinforcement contrast. A glossy clear coat may produce a broad continuous highlight above a subtler pattern; exposed teaching fibers may use a different surface. Do not assign raw conductor metalness merely because a carbon panel is dark and shiny.

Use geometry for trim thickness, ply-step cutaways and silhouette-changing chips. Keep microscopic filaments in shading detail or omit them at normal viewing distances. Do not extend an outer-ply weave unchanged around a cut edge as if every ply shared that orientation.

Let the viewer toggle woven/unidirectional specimens, expose a labeled ply inset and rotate the finish lighting. If rotating ply orientation changes a displayed pattern, retain the same specimen dimensions and avoid reporting stiffness without a separate calculation.
observable_checks: Inspect a hole and outer edge: both expose the finite shell thickness; the cosmetic face pattern does not wrap across the void.
Compare woven and unidirectional examples with finish held fixed: their declared reinforcement directions differ, while no fabricated strength readout appears.
In the teaching cutaway the number and thickness sum of displayed plies match the authored stack; hide the inset and retain the original outer surface.

known_limits: No laminate stiffness, failure, impact damage, cure process or structural suitability calculation. A visible weave cannot identify hidden plies; a cosmetic finish may obscure reinforcement.
Authored construction and prospective checks; no runtime artifact, render or material test has been executed for this record.
creative_affordances: A painted composite panel, matte technical specimen or glossy patterned shell can be valid choices. Keep a labeled construction inset when the chosen finish hides the underlying reinforcement.

claims.statement: Hexcel offers woven reinforcement fabrics and also describes nonwoven unidirectional carbon reinforcements; its product range therefore does not support treating all carbon reinforcement as a woven checker pattern.
claims.scope: Manufacturer reinforcement-form distinction only; laminate layup, resin finish and depiction choices are authored.
